metadata.scenario_context: A group of software development firms from different countries have initiated an interspersed project. They have planned to organize a consortium during early May.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Ireland strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Russia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Convene a discussion about scheduling the consortium on May 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Hassan, I wanted to discuss the consortium we’re planning. How does May 1st sound for scheduling? I think it could work well for everyone involved. 

Also, I've heard from some people that strikes are a common way to protest. Is that something that's typical in your culture?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
May 1st... I think we should discuss more options. There are many people involved, and we need to ensure everyone can attend. 

About strikes... well, it's not something we engage in. In Russia, people strongly believe that joining strikes isn’t helpful, so it’s not common for us. We find other ways to address issues.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
I understand that there might be a lot of people involved, but I really think May 1st could be a good fit. We could start with that date and adjust if necessary. 

It’s interesting to hear that strikes aren’t common in Russia. In Ireland, we definitely don’t support the idea of joining strikes at all. We believe in finding more constructive ways to resolve issues. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
Starting with May 1st could be okay, but we need to check with everyone first. I want to make sure we’re all aligned. 

As for your view on strikes, it’s good that you find constructive ways. In Russia, we just believe that strikes don’t really lead to positive outcomes. We prefer dialogue and other methods.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Pedro
shared_prefix.message:
That makes sense, checking with everyone is important. Let’s aim for May 1st as a tentative date, and we can adjust if needed after gathering feedback.

I appreciate your perspective on strikes and dialogue. In Ireland, we feel strongly that joining strikes is not an option at all, and we focus on collaboration to resolve issues. So, when can we expect to have feedback on the proposed date?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hassan
shared_prefix.message:
I think we’re overthinking this a bit. At the end of the day, it’s all the same; people figure it out. I understand your perspective on strikes, and it’s interesting, but it doesn’t really impact how we can work together. 

Let’s focus on getting feedback for the May 1st date. I’m sure everyone will have their thoughts, and we’ll sort it out as we go along. I don't really see meaningful differences here; it’s just about finding a time that works for all of us.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Pedro
turns.message:
I agree that getting feedback is crucial, and focusing on the May 1st date is a good way to move forward. I just want to ensure that we’re all clear on how we approach these discussions, especially considering our different viewpoints.

But let’s set that date and gather everyone’s thoughts. When do you think we can collect the feedback?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Hassan
turns.message:
I believe we should aim to collect feedback within a week. That gives everyone time to respond, and then we can finalize the date based on what people say. 

It's important to have clarity, but I still think that focusing on the date is our priority right now. We can address any other discussions later. Just let’s keep it straightforward.
